newsitem.title: FRANCE: EIB ecu-into-euro bond eligible for MATIF delivery.
newsitem.headline: EIB ecu-into-euro bond eligible for MATIF delivery.

text.p: French futures and options exchange MATIF said on Friday the 5.25 percent April 2004 Ecu bond first issued by the European Investment bank in January will be eligible for delivery into MATIF's June 1997 Ecu bond future.

MATIF said a group of Ecu experts had decided the bond was eligible for delivery as it satisfied today the criteria that more than one billion Ecus was outstanding and that bond had a maturity of between six and 10 years.
The EIB initially issued one billion Ecus of the bond on January 31 and added a further 300 million Ecu on February 19.
MATIF said the bond was currently considered eligible for delivery into its September 1997 Ecu bond future contract as well although a definitive ruling would be given on May 19.
It said the criteria for inclusion in the basket of eligible bonds were not automatic and the group of experts would issue its opinion for eligibility on a case by case basis.
MATIF also added the 5.50 percent April 2007 Ecu bond, or OAT, issued by France to the basket of eligible securities.

The EIB bond was described by the lead managers at the time of issue as a "euro" Eurobond. It will be paid in Ecu until such a time as a single European currency is launched and then it will be paid in euros.
